introduction: TexasLawHelp provides eviction information and a regional legal-aid directory. Choose legal help based on your county and case rather than treating an article as representation.
description: TexasLawHelp provides eviction information and a regional legal-aid directory. Choose legal help based on your county and case rather than treating an article as representatio

sections.who: Information is available publicly. Legal-aid organizations decide eligibility and case acceptance.
sections.get: Self-help resources and routes to legal assistance; the website does not guarantee an attorney.
sections.docs:
• Lease and landlord notices.
  • Court papers with hearing details.
  • Payment records and relevant messages.
sections.apply:
1. Find regional help

    Use the eviction referral page.

  2. Describe the case

    Give the provider your county, court date and notices.

  3. Follow intake instructions

    Ask whether representation or advice is available.
sections.after: Keep court dates visible while seeking help. Request guidance on your papers rather than assuming a referral changes the hearing.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using TexasLawHelp eviction and regional intake. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: The referral page lists legal-aid providers by geographic service area.
Does rent assistance equal legal representation?
They are different services; ask separately about each need.
The page links to eviction responses, appeals and related tenant issues.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
